Title: createReview — Happy Path (purchased product, first review) returns id, no validationErrors, status New
Preconditions: Runner-native. USER has >=1 Completed order with a product they have NOT yet reviewed on this store. Self-cleaning: the created review is deleted in Cleanup so the (user,product) pair stays reviewable next run.
Assertions:
[ERRORS label=create] errors[] empty
[DATA label=create] data.createReview.id is non-empty GUID
[COUNT label=create] data.createReview.validationErrors.length = 0
Cross_Layer_Checks: [ADMIN] Admin > Rating and reviews: the new review appears with Status = New (pending moderation) — createReview never auto-approves
Failure_Signals: createReview returns null id with a validationError on a genuinely eligible purchase; new review appears already Approved (should be New)

Title: createReview — INVALID_ENTITY_TYPE for non-Product entity
Preconditions: Runner-native. Reviews via xAPI are Product-only (ReviewValidator.IsProductReview). Any entityId works — the entity-type guard fires regardless of purchase.
Assertions:
[ERRORS label=create_vendor] errors[] empty
[NULL label=create_vendor] data.createReview.id
[DATA label=create_vendor] data.createReview.validationErrors.0.errorCode = INVALID_ENTITY_TYPE
Cross_Layer_Checks: [STOREFRONT] The storefront review widget hardcodes ENTITY_TYPE=Product, so a Vendor review is only reachable via a crafted API call — this case guards the server-side rule
Failure_Signals: createReview persists a Vendor review; validationErrors empty for entityType=Vendor

Title: createReview — PRODUCT_MUST_BE_PURCHASED when user has no completed order for the product
Preconditions: Runner-native. Discovers a catalog product the USER has NOT purchased (first search product; the user's completed-order products are a tiny subset, so a random catalog product is almost never purchased — the assertion tolerates the rare overlap via OR).
Assertions:
[ERRORS label=create_noorder] errors[] empty
[NULL label=create_noorder] data.createReview.id
[DATA label=create_noorder] data.createReview.validationErrors.0.errorCode = PRODUCT_MUST_BE_PURCHASED OR data.createReview.validationErrors.0.errorCode = DUPLICATE_REVIEW
Failure_Signals: createReview succeeds for a product the user never purchased

Title: createReview — DUPLICATE_REVIEW on second review of the same product
Preconditions: Runner-native. One review per user per product per store (ReviewValidator.ReviewExists). Creates one review, then attempts a second; both cleaned up.
Steps:
[AUTH role=USER]
[GQL-OP find_orders]
  query { orders(first: 20, filter: "status:Completed") { items { items { productId } } } }
[GQL-EXEC find_orders]
[GQL-CAPTURE find_orders.data.orders.items.0.items.0.productId → PID]
[GQL-OP create_first]
  mutation { createReview(command: { storeId: "{{STORE_ID}}" entityId: "{{PID}}" entityType: "Product" review: "AGENT-TEST first" rating: 5 }) { id validationErrors { errorCode } } }
[GQL-EXEC create_first]
[GQL-CAPTURE create_first.data.createReview.id → FIRST_ID]
[GQL-OP create_dup]
  mutation { createReview(command: { storeId: "{{STORE_ID}}" entityId: "{{PID}}" entityType: "Product" review: "AGENT-TEST duplicate" rating: 4 }) { id validationErrors { errorCode errorMessage } } }
[GQL-EXEC create_dup]
Assertions:
[ERRORS label=create_dup] errors[] empty
[NULL label=create_dup] data.createReview.id
[DATA label=create_dup] data.createReview.validationErrors.0.errorCode = DUPLICATE_REVIEW
Failure_Signals: second createReview for the same (user,product) persists a duplicate

Title: customerReviews — returns only Approved reviews (New/Rejected hidden)
Preconditions: Runner-native. Requires `npm run seed:reviews` — REVIEW_PRODUCT carries approved_count Approved reviews PLUS 1 New + 1 Rejected. The storefront query must return exactly the Approved ones, proving New+Rejected are hidden.
Assertions:
[ERRORS label=read] errors[] empty
[DATA label=read] data.customerReviews.totalCount = @td(REVIEW_PRODUCT.approved_count)
[COUNT label=read] data.customerReviews.items.length = @td(REVIEW_PRODUCT.approved_count)
Cross_Layer_Checks: [ADMIN] The seeded product also holds 1 New + 1 Rejected review (total 8 in admin) — the storefront returns only the Approved subset, so totalCount equals approved_count, NOT 8
Failure_Signals: New or Rejected reviews leak into the public items[] (totalCount > approved_count)

Title: customerReviews — pagination via first/after (PAGE_SIZE 5)
Preconditions: Runner-native. Requires `npm run seed:reviews` — REVIEW_PRODUCT has 6 Approved reviews (approved_count), so page 1 (first:5) returns 5 and page 2 (after:5) returns the remaining 1; totalCount is stable at approved_count on both pages.
Assertions:
[ERRORS label=page1] errors[] empty
[DATA label=page1] data.customerReviews.totalCount = @td(REVIEW_PRODUCT.approved_count)
[COUNT label=page1] data.customerReviews.items.length = 5
[DATA label=page1] data.customerReviews.pageInfo.hasNextPage = true
[ERRORS label=page2] errors[] empty
[DATA label=page2] data.customerReviews.totalCount = @td(REVIEW_PRODUCT.approved_count)
[COUNT label=page2] data.customerReviews.items.length >= 1
Failure_Signals: first:5 returns more or fewer than 5 items on page 1; totalCount differs between pages; page 2 empty despite 6 approved

Title: customerReviews — sort by created date descending
Preconditions: Runner-native. Requires `npm run seed:reviews` — REVIEW_PRODUCT has >=2 Approved reviews. sort=createddate:desc must return newest-first (item[0].createdDate >= item[1].createdDate).
Assertions:
[ERRORS label=sorted] errors[] empty
[DATA label=sorted] data.customerReviews.totalCount >= 2
[DATA label=sorted] data.customerReviews.items.0.createdDate >= data.customerReviews.items.1.createdDate
Cross_Layer_Checks: [EVIDENCE] createddate:desc = newest first; item[0] must be >= item[1]
Failure_Signals: sort returns oldest-first (item[0] older than item[1]) — wrong direction
